title: Research
text:
My research develops generalizable and trustworthy AI methods and applies them to complex scientific and societal problems. I work with heterogeneous, limited, and uncertain data, including images, sensor observations, satellite imagery, text, and geospatial information, to build models that hold up beyond their training data.



Diagram showing one research program, Generalizable and Trustworthy AI, branching into three tracks: machine learning from weak and multimodal data, AI for cybersecurity and AI safety, and AI for scientific and societal applications.




Generalizable & Trustworthy Machine Learning
Machine learning and AI methods that generalize beyond their training data and work with limited, heterogeneous, uncertain, or multimodal data.
Explore this track →


AI for Cybersecurity & AI Safety
Applying AI to cybersecurity, and building secure and trustworthy AI systems, including zero-day threat detection and LLM red teaming.
Explore this track →


AI for Scientific & Societal Applications
Data-driven methods for precision agriculture, environmental and climate analytics, and healthcare.
Explore this track →

title: CV
text:
Student Mentorship and Research Supervision
Since joining Grand Valley State University in 2023, I have supervised undergraduate and graduate research projects spanning machine learning and AI, data science, software engineering, healthcare, cybersecurity, and precision agriculture, several of which have led to scholarly publications and ongoing collaborations.

Undergraduate mentorship: Supervised four undergraduate capstone students and currently supervise one undergraduate research assistant on an MSGC-funded project mapping urban heat islands and environmental inequity in West Michigan.
Current thesis supervision: Supervise three graduate thesis students in CIS 695 working on Graph RAG models, obesity analytics for Michigan residents, and time-series deep learning models.
CIS 692, Master’s Capstone: Co-instructed and supervised four students in two industry-oriented teams developing a Google Earth Engine-based GIS and a deep learning system for colonoscopy polyp detection.
CIS 691, PSM Internship Supervision: Supervised five PSM interns on research-oriented projects in healthcare and precision agriculture, including dental implant failure prediction, precision agriculture sensor networks, and deep learning for skin disease detection. One project received the Best Project Award at the College of Computing Innovation Day (Health Informatics, Winter 2025).
CIS 693, Master’s Projects: Supervised 14 Master’s projects across software engineering, data science, machine learning, generative AI, precision agriculture, retail forecasting, and AI safety. One project received the Best Project Award at the College of Computing Innovation Day (Applied Computer Science, Winter 2026).

title: Md Kamrul Hasan
text:
About Me
I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of Information Sciences & Technologies at Grand Valley State University. My research focuses on artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative AI, and multimodal data analytics, with applications in precision agriculture, healthcare, environmental monitoring, and intelligent information systems.
My work explores how heterogeneous data—including text, images, sensor observations, satellite imagery, and geospatial information—can be integrated to develop practical and data-driven solutions to real-world problems. I am particularly interested in multimodal learning, predictive modeling, deep learning, and trustworthy AI.
I also enjoy teaching and mentoring students in machine learning, data science, and software engineering, and collaborating on interdisciplinary research that connects computing with real-world applications.
